# `aitbc genesis reset`

Reset the local chain: back up old data, generate a new genesis block, and restart services. This is a destructive operation. It stops the local blockchain services, backs up the chain data and environment, optionally creates a new genesis wallet, runs the genesis reset script, and restarts services. Use only when the current chain is being intentionally replaced.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc genesis reset [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--chain-id` | text | — | no | Chain ID (defaults to CHAIN_ID env or config) |
| `--new-wallet` | flag | `false` | no | Generate a new genesis wallet and update env files |
| `--yes` | flag | `false` | no | Skip confirmation prompt |
| `--data-dir` | path | — | no | Override chain data directory |
| `--etc-dir` | path | — | no | Override env directory |
| `--wallet-dir` | path | — | no | Override wallet directory |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc genesis reset
```
